lessons.title: Auto and Auto Ancillaries: Monthly Sales Data, Commodity Costs, and the EV Shift

body.text: Auto is the one sector where you do not have to wait for quarterly results to see how demand is doing. Companies publish unit sales on the first day of every month. But the headline dispatch number is what factories sent to dealers, not what customers bought. Learn to read past it, and add the two slower forces, commodity costs and the shift to electric, and you can analyse the sector ahead of most investors.

children.text: India is one of the world's largest markets for two-wheelers, tractors, and passenger vehicles. Auto and auto ancillary stocks such as Maruti Suzuki, Mahindra & Mahindra, Bajaj Auto, TVS Motor, Eicher Motors, Hero MotoCorp, Ashok Leyland, Bosch, Samvardhana Motherson, and MRF are widely held by retail investors and mutual funds. In Chapter 2 you saw that autos are cyclical with high operating leverage. This lesson adds the sector-specific tools.
Auto Is Really Five Different Businesses

children.text: These segments can move in opposite directions. Tractors can boom after a good monsoon while commercial vehicles slump as freight demand weakens. Ancillaries split further: a supplier to new vehicle factories rises and falls with production, while a tyre or battery company selling replacements in the aftermarket has steadier, more defensive demand, because every vehicle already on the road eventually needs new tyres.

markDefs.definition: Vehicles sent from a manufacturer's factory to its dealers. This is what companies report as monthly 'sales', and it is not the same as vehicles bought by customers.

children.text: Listed carmakers and two-wheeler companies report the previous month's unit sales to the stock exchanges around the first of each month. These numbers are

. The industry body SIAM compiles wholesale data across manufacturers. For actual customer purchases, look at retail registrations: the Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations (FADA) publishes monthly retail sales based on vehicle registrations recorded on the government's Vahan portal. The gap between the two tells you whether dealers are stocking up or clearing inventory.

columns.label: Wholesale (company data, SIAM)
points: Units shipped from factory to dealer
Released by companies around the first of each month
Can be pushed up ahead of festivals or to meet targets

columns.label: Retail (FADA, Vahan registrations)
points: Released a little later in the month
Hard to manipulate, since a vehicle must be registered to be driven

body.latex: \text{Closing dealer inventory} = \text{Opening inventory} + \text{Wholesale} - \text{Retail} \qquad \text{Inventory days} = \frac{\text{Closing inventory}}{\text{Retail sales} \div \text{Days in period}}
body.caption: Dealer inventory and how many days of sales it represents

body.title: How Much Stock Is Sitting With Dealers?
body.prompt: A two-wheeler maker's dealers start a 90-day quarter with 4,50,000 units in stock. During the quarter the company dispatches 10,50,000 units to dealers, and customers register 9,00,000 units. How many days of retail sales does closing dealer inventory represent?
body.explanation: Closing inventory = 4,50,000 + 10,50,000 - 9,00,000 = 6,00,000 units. Daily retail sales = 9,00,000 ÷ 90 = 10,000 units. Inventory days = 6,00,000 ÷ 10,000 = 60 days. Dealer stock rose from 45 days to 60 days. If retail demand does not pick up, the company will have to cut dispatches or offer discounts in coming months, hurting revenue and margins even though this quarter's reported 'sales' looked strong.

body.text: The Navratri to Diwali festive season is the most important selling period of the year, and manufacturers deliberately build dealer stock ahead of it. Strong wholesale numbers in August and September are normal. What matters is whether retail registrations during and after the festive period clear that stock. FADA's festive season retail reports are the numbers to watch.

body.title: The Record Dispatch Month
body.scenario: A passenger vehicle company reports record monthly dispatches, up 18% year on year, and the stock rises 4%. Two weeks later, FADA data shows passenger vehicle retail registrations for the industry grew only 3% in the same month. Dealer associations comment that inventory has climbed to well above normal levels, and several brands are offering higher discounts than last year.
body.prompt: How should you interpret the record dispatch number, and what do you expect over the next few months?
body.modelAnswer: The record dispatches mostly reflect stock being pushed into dealerships, not a surge in customer demand. With retail up only 3% against wholesale up 18%, dealer inventory is building, which is confirmed by high reported inventory levels and rising discounts. Over the next few months, expect one or more of: the company cutting dispatches to let dealers clear stock, which will show up as weak monthly 'sales' numbers; higher discounts, which reduce realisation per vehicle and margins; and possibly production cuts that lower utilisation and hurt operating leverage. The 4% stock rise on the headline was premature. Watch FADA retail data, reported inventory days, discount levels, and management commentary on dealer inventory in the next quarterly call.

children.text: For vehicle makers, raw materials and bought-out components typically make up the largest part of costs, often around 70% of revenue or more. The basket includes steel, aluminium, copper, rubber, plastics, and precious metals used in catalytic converters. When the basket rises, manufacturers raise vehicle prices, but usually with a lag and in steps, because buyers are price sensitive and competitors may hold prices. Ancillary suppliers often have contracts that pass commodity costs through to vehicle makers, but typically with a delay of a quarter or so.

body.title: Illustrative Cost Structure of a Car Manufacturer (% of Revenue)
The Commodity Hit Before Price Hikes
body.prompt: Using the illustrative cost structure above, raw materials are 72% of revenue and EBITDA margin is 12%. If the raw material basket becomes 5% more expensive and the company has not yet raised vehicle prices, by how many percentage points does EBITDA margin fall?
body.explanation: Margin impact = 72% × 5% = 3.6 percentage points, taking EBITDA margin from 12% to 8.4%. That is a 30% fall in EBITDA from a 5% rise in input costs. To fully offset it, the company needs a price increase of roughly 3.6% of revenue, which is why auto companies announce price hikes soon after commodity rallies, and why margins recover only as those hikes take effect.

children.text: The EV Shift: Winners, Losers, and Timing

Electric vehicle adoption in India is uneven across segments. Three-wheelers, especially passenger and cargo rickshaws, have electrified fastest because running costs matter enormously to commercial users. Electric two-wheelers have reached a meaningful single-digit share of the market, with new listed players such as Ola Electric and Ather Energy competing against incumbents like TVS Motor and Bajaj Auto. Electric passenger cars remain a small share of sales. Government support has shifted over time, from the FAME schemes to the PM E-DRIVE scheme launched in 2024, and each change in subsidy levels has visibly affected monthly EV sales.

body.caption: How the EV Shift Affects Auto Ancillaries

cells: At risk
Engine parts, pistons, fuel injection systems, exhaust systems, conventional gearboxes
Electric vehicles have no internal combustion engine and far fewer moving parts in the drivetrain
Largely neutral
Tyres, seats, lighting, glass, brakes, steering, body panels
Needed by every vehicle regardless of powertrain
Beneficiaries
Battery packs and cells, electric motors, motor controllers, power electronics, wiring harnesses, thermal management
New content per vehicle that does not exist in petrol and diesel vehicles

body.title: Which Supplier Faces the Biggest EV Risk?
body.question: Four auto ancillary companies each earn most of their revenue from one product line. Whose long-term revenue is most threatened if EV adoption accelerates?
options: A tyre maker selling mostly to the replacement market
A maker of fuel injection systems for petrol and diesel engines
body.explanation: Fuel injection systems exist only in internal combustion engines, so each vehicle that goes electric removes that content entirely. Tyres and lighting are needed by all vehicles, and EVs typically need more wiring and electronics, not less. The pace of the shift still matters: a strong ICE-focused supplier can generate cash for many years, especially in segments and export markets where adoption is slow.

body.text: Do not treat the EV shift as a single date. Adoption depends on segment, battery costs, charging infrastructure, and subsidies. Ask each company what share of its revenue is powertrain-agnostic, what share is ICE-specific, and what it is doing to win EV content, rather than labelling the whole sector winners or losers.

body.title: Fill in the Blank
body.textWithBlank: The monthly 'sales' numbers auto companies report on the first of the month are ___ dispatches to dealers, while FADA publishes retail registrations.
body.explanation: Reported monthly sales are units shipped to dealers. Retail registrations show what customers actually bought, and the gap reveals changes in dealer inventory.

body.title: Monthly and Quarterly Auto Tracking Routine
steps: Around the first of each month, note dispatches for your holdings by segment, including domestic and exports separately
When FADA data is released, compare retail registration growth with wholesale growth for the same segment
Estimate whether dealer inventory is building or clearing, and read dealer association commentary on inventory and discounts
Track steel, aluminium, copper, and rubber prices, and look for announced vehicle price increases
In quarterly results, check realisation per vehicle, gross margin, and EBITDA margin against commodity trends
Follow EV share in each segment and any changes to government incentives
For ancillaries, split revenue into new vehicle supply, replacement, exports, and ICE-specific versus powertrain-agnostic products

points: Auto is several businesses: two-wheelers, passenger vehicles, commercial vehicles, tractors, and ancillaries, each with different demand drivers
Monthly company sales are wholesale dispatches to dealers; FADA's retail registrations show real customer demand
A widening gap between wholesale and retail builds dealer inventory, which usually leads to cut dispatches or higher discounts later
Raw materials are often around 70% of a vehicle maker's revenue, so commodity rallies squeeze margins until price hikes catch up
EV adoption is fastest in three-wheelers, meaningful in two-wheelers, and still small in passenger cars
The EV shift threatens ICE-specific ancillaries, leaves powertrain-agnostic parts largely unaffected, and creates new content in batteries, motors, and electronics

body.text: Cost structure, inventory, and commodity examples use illustrative figures. EV adoption levels and government schemes change frequently; refer to Vahan, FADA, SIAM, and the Ministry of Heavy Industries for current data. Company names are examples, not recommendations to buy or sell any security.
